subject: Performance SLO follow-up: concurrency, streaming & rate limits
messages:
From: Emma Lawson <emma@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-05T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Quick follow-up on today's SLO discussion

Marissa — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can scope a PoC:

- What we ran through on the call: FintechCo plans to use Redwood for real-time fraud scoring embedded in several user flows. We expect sustained traffic with peaks.
- Target SLOs: 95th percentile latency target for streaming responses ~< 350ms end-to-end (client -> Redwood -> model -> client).
- Throughput/volume: average 600 RPS, peak bursts up to ~1,200 RPS for short windows (a few minutes). Typical request payload ~400 tokens in + ~150 tokens out, streamed to clients.
- Concurrency question: we expect up to ~800 parallel inference requests at peak that will be actively streaming. We want to understand the best practice for connection pooling/HTTP keep-alive vs opening many connections, and whether Redwood imposes per-connection concurrent stream limits.
- Rate-limit negotiation: what levers do we have for hosted vs dedicated? Can we get a temporary quota increase for PoC?

Can you confirm the default hosted rate limits and recommended connection pooling strategy? Also, can you share a simple SLO template we can fill out (latency buckets, traffic shape)?

Thanks — will loop in SRE if we need to share topology.

—Emma
Emma Lawson
Head of Integrations, FintechCo
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Emma Lawson <emma@fintechco.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-06T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up on today's SLO discussion

Hi Emma — great speaking earlier. Appreciate the clear targets. Short answers up front, then next steps and attachments.

Short answers:
- Default hosted rate limits: our baseline is 600 requests/sec per org for standard API keys, with short burst capacity up to ~1,200 req/sec for a few minutes. We can request a temporary uplift for PoC ahead of contract.
- Concurrency model: Redwood treats each incoming request as a discrete inference unit. For streaming (SSE/chunked), the connection remains open while the model emits tokens; a single TCP connection can support multiple logical streams depending on protocol (HTTP/2 multiplexing or websockets). For HTTP/1.1 chunked streaming we recommend keeping per-connection concurrency moderate.
- Recommended pool sizing (rule of thumb): pool_size = ceil(expected_parallel_streams / per_connection_streams). For many customers we recommend starting with 8–12 streams per HTTP/2 connection.

Notes attached: I've included a filled SLO template and a sample network topology figure. Rishi, can you add any technical limits or PoC constraints?

Next steps:
1) Rishi to provide ops/SE guidance on per-connection behavior and any model-specific throughput knobs.
2) We'll provision a temporary quota increase for your PoC (proposed: 1,500 concurrent requests for 2 weeks) once we agree on test dates.
3) Fill out the attached SLO template (I put baseline numbers from today's call).
4) Schedule a PoC run this month — propose Wed 18th or Thu 19th for a 3-hour intensive run.

I've copied Neha for commercial/quote alignment.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Emma Lawson <emma@fintechco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-06T12:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up on today's SLO discussion

Emma — adding some technical detail from the SE side. TL;DR: your targets are achievable; a short PoC will validate tuning.

Technical guidance:
- Protocols: If you can use HTTP/2, we get multiplexing benefits and can support ~8–12 concurrent streams per connection reliably. Websockets also work but require separate handling for connection lifecycle. HTTP/1.1 chunked streaming is fine, but you'll need more parallel connections to reach the same concurrency.
- Per-connection streams: plan for 8 streams/conn as conservative default; if your client stack supports robust HTTP/2 multiplexing, plan for 12 streams/conn and validate under load.
- Rate limits & quotas: hosted defaults (600 req/sec) are soft for PoC; we can open to 1,500 concurrent requests for a limited window. For production we typically recommend Dedicated capacity when sustained concurrency >1,000 req/sec and tight latency SLOs under 300ms.
- Connection pooling: keep-alive is essential. Use a connection pool sized to expected_streams / streams_per_conn + headroom (e.g., for 800 concurrent streams with 8 streams/conn => pool of 100 connections, add 20% headroom => 120).
- Token throughput: with your estimate (400 in + 150 out avg) your token/s target at 800 parallel streams is ~(550 tokens/request * requests/sec) if requests/sec = concurrency * avg_req_per_second_per_stream. We'll verify numbers in PoC.

PoC constraints and requirements:
- We ask that you provide a realistic traffic generator (we can share a script) and a representative prompt set.
- We'll collect server and client-side traces, token-level metrics, and latency percentiles.
- We'll schedule a time window for the quota bump and monitor together.

I'll prepare a short PoC runbook and load script.

—Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Emma Lawson <emma@fintechco.com>

Subject: Re: Quick follow-up on today's SLO discussion

Thanks — that is helpful. A few clarifications from SRE:

- We'll be using HTTP/2 with SSE-style streaming from the client. Good to hear 12 streams/conn is reasonable.
- Confirmed peak target: 800 parallel streaming inferences, sustained for a rolling 10-minute window as a realistic stress pattern for checkout spikes.
- Latency SLO: 95th < 350ms end-to-end is firm for the product launch.
- Token volume: typical combined tokens/request ~550. Approx target token throughput ~120k tokens/sec during peak.

Please share the PoC runbook and the sample load generator. Also confirm the proposed temporary quota: 1,500 concurrent requests for 2 weeks (we only need 2–3 hours of coordinated windows but would prefer flexibility).

—Emma
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

2) SE lead: Rishi will own the runbook and load-generator setup. Expect an initial runbook link and load script by EOD tomorrow.
3) Connection pooling guidance: start with 8 streams/connection conservative, aim for 12 if your client stack behaves well. We'll validate during PoC and adjust.
4) Commercial: Neha will follow up with a short-term quote and outline Dedicated options if sustained throughput requires it.
5) Actions for FintechCo: please fill the attached SLO template and share network egress IPs for firewall allowlisting.
